cards.title: Declutter the map: colleagues live in the coin tray; Owner view groups by owner
cards.detail:
Both Domain view and Owner view carry a full row of colleague furniture — colleague buildings, the campfire, and four locked bench seats — across the neutral middle of the map. That furniture predates the coin tray (RavenBench), which is now a fixed top bar on every tab (the Map tab included) and is already the agent action surface: a coin fires plays today. With the tray in place, the map no longer needs to host colleagues.

Decisions (director, 2026-07-13):
- Domain view loses the entire landmark row: colleague buildings, campfire, and locked seats.
- Owner view works exactly like Domain view (same work-geography — contexts, projects, systems, stray piles) except each region is labelled and grouped by its owner (e.g. 'DANVERS', from domain.owner with the human:/colleague: prefix stripped) instead of its domain name (e.g. 'SOFTWARE'). Ownership is not assumed 1:1 with domains: a domain may map to a single owner (then the two views differ only in the label), or ownership may regroup regions.
- The two features the colleague building overlay carried — the work journal and the Needs-a-Human lane — move onto the colleague's coin as coin actions.
- The colleague-level escalation cue moves with them: a coin glows or badges when its colleague has a Needs-a-Human item or an overdue/unhealthy system, preserving the at-a-glance signal the building glow used to give. Tile-level Needs-a-Human glow stays on the work tile (L1) unchanged.

Scope:
- Domain-view layout: stop rendering the colleague/seat/campfire landmark layer (MapLandmarks renders in both modes today; skip the whole row in Domain view).
- Owner view: reuse the Domain-view work layout; label and group regions by domain.owner rather than name; keep an owner-less region visibly unclaimed (demand signal, plan §1.2).
- Coin (RavenBench): add Journal and Needs-a-Human actions to the coin action menu; wire the coin lit/activated state to a colleague-level escalation rollup.

Out of scope:
- Placement UX for unplaced projects (tracked separately, in flight).
- The long-term question of whether the map becomes purely work and whether Owner view survives — noted in the Map Glow Up thread, not decided here.
